Lets the app see which app is in front, to time the cards per app and to gate the apps you chose. Nothing leaves your phone.

A card pops up every so often, only while the screen is on and unlocked, never on the lock screen. Answer it and you\'re done, or keep going. A card you don\'t touch is withdrawn, so its time doesn\'t count.
None. For example a card every 5 minutes on your biggest time wasters, or never on your maps app.
Show the note\'s fields under the answer
On the full-screen card: every field of the note the card didn\'t show, such as the meaning or the reading, so a definition left off the card\'s back is still there.
Pass records Good and Fail records Again. Hard and Easy are never offered, anywhere in the app.
Ask for cards before chosen apps
Opening one of them first asks for a few cards. Pass or Fail, each answer counts. No grace period: close the app and open it again, and it asks again. Nothing due means no gate.
While a Bluetooth device is connected
Everything pauses: no cards, and the gate is open. For example in the car or with headphones at work.
Without the \"Nearby devices\" permission, only Bluetooth audio (car, headphones, speakers) is detected, not watches or keyboards.
No cards while Do Not Disturb or another mode silences notifications.
No cards while you are in a call.
None. For example no cards from 22:00 to 07:00.
Pause while my PC is in use
With Micro Review Desktop, the Anki add-on, on your PC: cards and the gate pause for 5 minutes after you last use its mouse or keyboard.
In Anki on your PC: Tools › Micro Review Desktop. Type the pairing code shown there.
Pause while my PC is in use
No cards, the gate is open, for 5 minutes after you last use your PC\'s mouse or keyboard. Your PC tells the phone through ntfy.sh, a free relay: only a number of seconds is sent.
Answers wait to be synced: as your next card screen closes, or now. Asked last: %1$s.

Nothing waiting. Asked AnkiDroid last: %1$s. AnkiDroid only syncs with its screen up for a moment, so it\'s only asked as a card screen closes, hidden behind it. Cards your PC reviewed are skipped until then.

Cards, the gate, pauses and the look
What the monitor sees and did, to tell why a card or the gate didn\'t come.

Lie on your stomach, hands under your shoulders. Push your chest up while your hips stay on the floor and your back stays relaxed, then lower. Go a little higher each time, as far as is comfortable. The main tool: morning, evening, and whenever the leg acts up.
On hands and knees, back flat. Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back, level with your body, without letting your back sag or twist. Hold, come back, switch.
On your side, elbow under your shoulder, knees bent. Lift your hips until you\'re straight from knees to head. Hold, lower.
On your back, one knee bent, the other leg straight, hands under the small of your back. Lift your head and shoulders a little, as one block: no curling of the neck or the lower back. Hold, lower.
On your back, knees bent, feet flat. Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips until you\'re straight from shoulders to knees, without arching. Hold, lower slowly.

Stand with soft knees. Push your hips back as if closing a car door behind you, chest forward, back straight. Come up by squeezing your glutes. This is how you bend: for socks, the floor, the dishwasher.
Standing tall or lying on your back: glide your head straight back, making a double chin, eyes level, until the back of your neck lengthens. Hold, relax. Against a head that drifts forward.
Arms by your sides. Draw your shoulder blades back and down, toward your back pockets, without shrugging or arching. Hold, relax.
Forearm on a door frame, elbow at shoulder height. Step through gently until the front of your chest stretches. Ribs down, no arching.
Head, upper back and hips against a wall, feet a step out. Arms in a W against the wall: slide them up to a Y and back down, only as far as they stay on the wall.

Kneel on one knee on a cushion, the other foot in front. Tuck your tailbone under and squeeze the glute of the kneeling side, then shift forward a little until the front of that hip stretches. Don\'t arch your back. For a pelvis that tips forward.

Lie on your side, bottom knee bent. Top leg straight, toes pointing forward, not up. Lift it a hand\'s height, slightly behind your body, and lower slowly. The side of the hip that keeps knees and feet tracking straight.
Foot flat, sitting or standing. Without curling your toes, draw the ball of your foot toward your heel so the arch lifts. Hold, relax. With feet pointing forward when you walk, against duck feet.
Feet apart, hands on your lower back. Lean back gently from the waist, hips forward, as far as is comfortable, and come back up. The quick undo after sitting.
Get up and walk: to the kitchen, around the room, up the stairs. Stand tall, feet pointing forward.
Stand tall, a hand on something for balance. Rise onto your toes, pause, lower slowly.
Long step stance, back heel up. Tuck your tailbone under and squeeze the back glute until the front of that hip stretches. Stay tall.
On your side, elbow under your shoulder, legs straight and stacked. Lift your hips into one straight line and hold. Hold longer as it gets easy.
Hands under your shoulders, body in one straight line: lower your chest, push back up. Start with your hands on a counter, then a chair, then the floor.
Sit back to a chair with a hip hinge, touch it lightly, stand up through your heels. A lower seat as it gets easy; no deep squats under load yet.
One foot forward, one back, upright. Lower the back knee only as far as feels fine, push back up through the front foot.
A band around a door handle, or a loaded backpack with your free hand on a table and your back flat. Pull your elbow back to your ribs, shoulder blade back, lower slowly.
Like the glute bridge with one foot on the floor and the other knee pulled in. Lift and lower without your hips tipping.
A backpack or light dumbbells held close. Hinge as practiced, back flat, down to just below the knees, up by squeezing your glutes. Add weight only when the next morning is no worse.
Carry one heavy bag in one hand and walk tall without leaning. Switch hands.
Morning check-in, an evening routine, stand-up breaks from the PC

A check-in and press-ups when you wake, a short routine in the evening, stand-up breaks from the PC add-on while you sit. Prompted like the cards, when you\'re on your phone. Off until you pick a program.
For disc-related back or leg pain (sciatica): press-ups, spine-sparing core work, walking, posture work that loads nothing.
Strength three days a week, bodyweight first, with the same core and posture work.
A self-care routine, not a diagnosis or treatment. If things stop improving or get worse, see a physio; a McKenzie-trained one suits back pain like this.
Rehab set, then posture · about 15 min
Bead: evening done. Dot: where the leg pain reached that morning, darker lower.
Extension, spine-sparing core work, walking, and posture work that loads nothing.
Strength every other day at most: bodyweight in weeks 1 and 2, light loads from week 3. The recovery set stays as the warm-up. Week %1$d.

No heavy lifting.
No deep squats or crouching under load.
No bending forward with a rounded lower back under load.
No twisting under load.
No hamstring stretching, sit-ups, crunches or toe touches.
No bending forward in the first hour after waking.
Ready to rebuild when the leg pain stays above the knee, mornings are easy, and nothing has flared for a couple of weeks. Bring things back one at a time.
Start Rebuild? Strength comes in every other day, bodyweight first. You can go back to Recovery any time.
From the PC add-on after 25 minutes of sitting, one at a time, in this order.

Discomfort up to 3–4 out of 10 is fine if it's no worse the next morning.
Pain moving up toward the back is a good sign. Pain moving back down the leg and staying a few days: back off to the rehab set.
Bend with a hip hinge. Break up sitting every 20–30 minutes.
Brace for sneezes and coughs: stand tall, slight arch.
Walk with your feet pointing forward and push off the big toe.
Strength needs fuel: protein at every meal and a little more food than feels normal. Without dairy: eggs, fish, meat, tofu, lentils, pea or soy protein.
Numbness in the groin or inner thighs, changes in bladder or bowel control, foot weakness or foot drop, or symptoms in both legs.
Morning: at the first unlock after a night. Evening: from the time set, while you\'re on your phone. Held back during calls, Do Not Disturb, a Bluetooth pause and a snooze.
The pain has reached the knee or lower three mornings running after being higher: back off to the rehab set only. If it stays there, see a physio.
Worse this morning after yesterday\'s strength session: keep today to the rehab set, and go lighter next time.
First hour after waking: no bending forward. Hinge at the hips; for socks, sit and bring the foot up.
Where does the leg pain reach this morning?
%1$s. Floor space and a few minutes.
